claim: A retiree who keeps savings in 3-month Treasury bills and spends only the interest has a principal that never falls, but an income that tracks the bill rate. The average bill yield fell from 4.353% in 2007 to 0.15% in 2009, cutting that income by 96.6%, and stayed below 0.25% for 7 straight years (2009-2015). It happened again from 2019 (2.061%) to 2021 (0.044%), a 97.9% cut, before recovering to 4.967% in 2024. Across 90 starting years from 1934 to 2023, interest income fell by more than half within two years 15 times, and in 14 of 92 calendar years it was below 0.25% of principal.

assumptions: Interest income on a fixed principal is proportional to the annual average 3-month bill yield (bills rolled continuously; discount-basis yield used as quoted).
No taxes, no inflation adjustment (the comparison is of nominal income on unchanged principal), no reinvestment of interest.
